cards.title: Exposure-Response Scatterplot and Time-Order Display Conventions
cards.claim: Exposure-response scatter and a time-ordered paired concentration-response loop are distinct displays. A loop requires verified time-matched pairs from the same serial observation subject and compatible context; shared experimental-unit or group identity is insufficient. A loop can suggest time dependence, but its appearance alone identifies neither a specific mechanism nor a model.
conditions: An individual loop requires verified within-subject concentration-response pairing and order.
A separately documented shared regimen exposure may support labelled regimen-assigned scatter without individual PK pairing; never fabricate nearest-time joins.
The display is exploratory, not a model fit or causal identification.
required_inputs: Scatter branch: a supplied qualified exposure metric (e.g. concentration, AUC or Cmax) with source, unit, concentration basis and exposure window, and a measured response with endpoint, unit, reference and response time/window.

Documented individual linkage or explicit shared regimen/group exposure assignment; preserve observation-level IDs and nesting. Unknown independent-unit n stays unknown rather than blocking otherwise qualified record-level scatter.

Loop branch only: time-matched concentration and response with verified serial_observation_subject_id, study/regimen/assay context, measurement timestamps and documented pairing/time-alignment method; no invented nearest-time joins.

Preserve X and Y quantification/censoring/missingness statuses, units and applicable bounds separately. Numeric values are required only for quantitative points; unmatched and censored records stay visible in a companion status/count table.
Optional exposure uncertainty or response summary/error inputs only when supplied or explicitly qualified, with their statistic, scale, unit level and source.
limitations: A visible loop does not prove a specific PK/PD model structure.
Absence of a loop does not prove a direct effect.
Unpaired data cannot be forced into a loop display.
This is an engineering display contract, not a regulatory mandate.
cards.downstream_use: Prioritize later time-course or mechanistic model evaluation based on observed time-dependence.

plot_recipe.input_contract: Choose scatter or within-subject loop explicitly. Scatter requires a supplied qualified exposure metric (concentration, AUC, Cmax or another defined metric) with X source/unit/basis/window and a measured response with Y source/endpoint/unit/reference/time-window, plus documented individual linkage or shared regimen assignment. Only a loop requires verified serial_observation_subject_id, paired concentration and response timestamps, documented time-alignment and order within compatible study/regimen/assay context. Preserve X/Y status and bounds separately; numeric values only for quantitative records. Unknown independent-unit n remains labelled unknown. Optional uncertainty layers need supplied or explicitly qualified inputs.
plot_recipe.plot_type: Exposure-response scatter; a time-ordered concentration-response loop only when time-matched within-unit observations are verified. Optional concentration-time and response-time companion panels are separate.
plot_recipe.axes_and_units: X = supplied qualified exposure metric with basis/unit/window; Y = measured response with endpoint/unit/reference/time. For a hysteresis display specifically X = time-matched concentration and Y = response, with arrows or colour indicating verified observation order. A time-X dual-Y display is not the hysteresis loop.
plot_recipe.grouping_and_connections: Require documented linkage within study, individual/regimen, endpoint and compatible assay/time context. Never create closest-row or nearest-time pairs. A supplied shared regimen exposure can be plotted against individual responses only when assignment is known and labelled shared; it is not independent individual PK. For a loop connect only verified ordered pairs, with recorded gaps explicit. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
plot_recipe.point_and_summary_layers: Preserve observed values as points at their actual record level. Keep raw observations separate from optional source-reported or explicitly defined descriptive summaries. A labelled group-summary guide is not an individual trajectory. Do not reconstruct individuals from a mean and SD.
plot_recipe.censoring_and_missingness: Preserve X exposure and Y response statuses separately with their units, windows and documented bounds. A censored concentration has its own assay bound; it does not automatically define a bound for derived AUC or another exposure metric. Do not turn a censored X or Y into an exact paired loop point. Display documented inequalities or separate status records, retain unmatched-pair counts/reasons, and do not silently infer a pair from nearest timestamps.
plot_recipe.transformations_and_formula: Retain original values, units, formula, input linkage and calculation order. Perform only the explicitly stated descriptive transformation with complete compatible inputs. No model fitting, integration, unsampled-peak interpolation or arbitrary log offsets.
plot_recipe.uncertainty_and_n: Distinguish independent PK units, PD units and repeated/nested responses. If supplied and compatible, horizontal intervals describe exposure uncertainty and vertical intervals describe the stated response statistic; response spread is not exposure-estimation uncertainty. No invented or universally banned uncertainty bars.
plot_recipe.interpretation_limits: A visible loop may motivate several time-dependent hypotheses; it does not identify one mechanism. No visible loop does not establish a direct effect. No model selection, fitted Emax, target estimation or clinical conclusion follows from this scatter alone.
plot_recipe.stop_or_fallback: Keep unmatched/censored-pair counts and reasons in a companion table. Missing individual pairing blocks a within-unit loop, not separately qualified regimen-level scatter. A dose-response plot may be useful but must not be relabelled concentration-response. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
plot_recipe.implementation_conventions: This recipe is an explicitly reviewed engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law. Use readable legends, separate aligned panels and visible status/count annotations. No universal numeric completeness threshold. No change to source data or current project Rules.

claim_support.claim: Exposure-response information can be used to examine responses at various concentrations attained over time, and hysteresis may result from delayed or persistent clinical measurements compared to plasma concentrations.
claim_support.scope: General guidance on time-dependent responses and hysteresis.

claim_support.claim: The FDA guidance explains the value of within-individual concentration-response time courses for reducing the specific confounding from inter-individual PK variability and dose-selection/titration; this does not establish freedom from every possible time-varying confounder.

The most appropriate representation of exposure depends on study objectives; if response varies with time within a dosage interval, relating response to concentration within individual subjects retrieves maximum information.
claim_support.scope: Selection of exposure metrics based on time-dependence.
